rows.grounds: direct object of the imperative; refers to the immortal essence
compound in apposition to amṛtaṃ; kaula + sadbhāva

items.question: What essential nature characterizes the Kaula nectar that the listener is commanded to hear?
premises: The listener is commanded to hear.
The object to be heard is nectar.
This nectar is identified as the true nature of Kaula.
That Kaula true nature is essenced as Kāmakalā.
items.inference: The Kaula nectar to be heard is essentially constituted by Kāmakalā.
uncertainties: The precise doctrinal sense of kāmakalā in this context is not fully specified by the verse alone.
items.plain_english: Hear the nectar, the true nature of Kaula, whose essence is Kāmakalā.
